messages:
Marta López: Thinking aloud — customers keep asking to restrict which model tiers certain roles can call (cost/PD controls). Proposal: a routing-policy <> RBAC binding so roles can be allowlisted/denied for model groups + optional per-role quotas. Thoughts?

Kenji Sato: +1 on need. We already have routing policies by tenancy, but not identity scopes. Curious where enforcement lives: gateway (fast reject) or runtime (fine-grained)?

Samir Patel: My vote: reject early at the API gateway for latency and cost signals, but enforce as a second check in the router to prevent bypass. Gateway can do a cheap allow/deny based on token -> role lookup.

Anya Vasilieva: UX note: customers want one view — a matrix that shows roles x model-tiers with editable cells for allow/deny and quota sliders. Also surface "expected monthly spend" estimate per role when toggling tiers. Would reduce admin surprises. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Roland Briggs: Backend implications: we need to store bindings and quotas per tenant + per-role. Migration path for existing tenants is default-allow today; should default to "inherit" to avoid sudden breakage. Also need audit entries for every override.

Kenji Sato: Example API payload (rough):
```json
{
  "role_id": "billing_admin",
  "bindings": [
    {"model_group": "open-llama-large", "allow": true, "monthly_token_limit": 500000},
    {"model_group": "opt-tier-2", "allow": false}
  ]
}
```
This could be surfaced in Console but enforced at gateway with a small cache.

Samir Patel: Important: fallback policy when a role is denied for a requested model. Do we fail with 403 or auto-fallback to a cheaper compatible model (if flagged)? Product tradeoff.

Marta López: Recommend default behavior: 403 + clear error and telemetry event. Add an optional toggle per-binding: "allow-fallback-to: model_group_id" for orgs that want graceful degradation.

Anya Vasilieva: For Console: prefer an inline "preview cost impact" modal when editing bindings. And add a telemetry tile to the role detail page showing per-role API call counts, tokens, and spend in last 30d. That ties to billing and makes RBAC changes less scary.

Kenji Sato: For implementation: gateway needs sub-100µs check. Suggest a compact policy cache keyed by (tenant, role) storing a bitset of allowed model_group IDs + token quota counters stored in Redis with windowed buckets.

Roland Briggs: Agree. Also need an events pipeline name for telemetry: rbac.routing.allow_check and rbac.routing.denied (include reason/fallback). These feed Console dashboards and alerts.

Samir Patel: Small infra caveat: quota enforcement across dedicated pools is harder — cross-pool counters required or enforce at tenant-level only. We'll document limitations in v1.

Marta López: Action items:
- Kenji: prototype gateway cache + check (P0)
- Anya: mockups for matrix + role detail usage tile (P0)
- Roland: schema + migration plan + telemetry event spec (P1)
- Samir: notes on quota enforcement edge cases + fallback design (P1)

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: feature/routing-rbac-proto -> staging at 2025-08-08T18:30:00Z :rocket:

Kenji Sato: I'll push a toy payload and a tiny middleware today so we can iterate with the UI mocks.

Marta López: Thanks everyone — let's try to keep initial scope narrow: allow/deny + preview cost. No auto-fallback in v1 unless customer opts in. :thumbsup:

Roland Briggs: +1

Anya Vasilieva: +1

Samir Patel: 👍
